Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source was originally cited. Trade press (May 2026) shows commercial 4G only launched in CAR in 2025 (Telecel, joining Orange and Moov Africa) and remains largely confined to Bangui, with overall internet penetration only ~12% and 2G/3G (not 4G) covering ~60% of population in 2024 per GSMA Mobile Connectivity Index. The original 64% figure appears to have wrongly applied a GSMA sub-regional 'Central Africa' 4G-expansion statistic to the country itself. Revised down to <25% (code 1).

revision_notes: No source originally cited. Confirmed via AWS's official region list that the only African region is af-south-1 (Cape Town, South Africa); no evidence of a Microsoft Azure or Google Cloud availability zone in Central Africa or a nearer sub-region. Original code 2 (served remotely from a distant region) is supported and left unchanged.

Definition: Whether the government has established dedicated data center infrastructure and/or a government cloud (G-Cloud) strategy for hosting e-government services and public sector data domestically. Critical for data sovereignty and e-government service delivery.
Value Name: No government data center or cloud strategy
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source originally cited. The AU's PIDA programme lists an active project to build a government data centre in CAR (part of a six-country ECCAS data-exchange initiative), and Central African ministries signed a 2021 agreement with the Cybastion Institute of Technology to construct government data centres. This indicates a strategy/project at planning stage rather than 'no strategy'. Revised from 1 to 2 (planned/under construction); implementation status is unconfirmed — recommend human review, as sources are a regional investment brochure and a single 2021 news item with no evidence of completion.

Africa's startup scene is well-documented by trackers like Partech, Disrupt Africa, and Briter Bridges.
Value Name: Nascent (very few tech startups, no visible VC activity)
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source originally cited. No VC funding activity for CAR is recorded in African VC trackers (Africa: The Big Deal, Partech, Disrupt Africa do not list CAR). Found only small donor-funded accelerator cohorts (a 20-participant US State Department/George Mason University accelerator, 2021) and an unfunded AI-hub partnership announcement (2025) with no VC involvement. Code 1 (nascent, no visible VC activity) is confirmed.

This is evidence of at least one to two identifiable hubs rather than none. Definition: The size and vibrancy of the local software developer and technology professional community. Measured through proxies such as GitHub activity, Stack Overflow representation, local tech meetup groups, and developer surveys. Indicates the country's capacity to build and maintain digital systems locally.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source originally cited. Individual GitHub and LinkedIn profiles confirm a handful of developers based in Bangui and a few small local software firms (web development, .NET/MERN stack), but CAR does not appear in GitHub Octoverse, the Stack Overflow Developer Survey, or AfriLabs developer counts, and no quantified community-size figure exists. Code 1 (negligible, very few active developers) is confirmed as the best-supported estimate; recommend human review given the informal, low-quality sourcing available (individual profiles, directory-style blogs).

Definition: The proportion of the population with basic digital skills (ability to use a computer, smartphone, or the internet for simple tasks such as sending messages, finding information, or using apps). Based on ITU household survey data, Afrobarometer, or national ICT surveys.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source originally cited. No direct ITU/Afrobarometer basic-digital-skills survey exists for CAR, so — consistent with the original methodology of inferring literacy from the internet-use rate — the freshest World Bank/ITU figure for individuals using the internet is 13.8% (2024, up from 13.84% in 2023), above the earlier ~10% estimate. This crosses the threshold into the 10-24% band. Revised from 1 to 2; this remains a proxy rather than a direct literacy measurement, so recommend human review if a direct ITU digital-skills indicator becomes available.

Definition: The gap between men and women in mobile internet usage or internet access. Based on the GSMA Mobile Gender Gap data or ITU gender-disaggregated ICT statistics. A smaller gap indicates more equitable access to digital opportunities.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source originally cited. No CAR-specific gender-gap survey exists; the original score used a Sub-Saharan Africa regional proxy (>30% gap). GSMA's Mobile Gender Gap Report 2025 puts the SSA regional mobile-internet gender gap at 29% for 2024 (down from 32% in 2023 and 36% in 2022). This moves the regional proxy from the 'large gap' (30-40%) band into the 'moderate gap' (20-29%) band. Revised from 2 to 3; flagged for human review as this remains a regional estimate, not a CAR-specific figure.

Value Name: Very limited (<2 institutions with ICT programmes)
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No source originally cited. The University of Bangui's Institut Supérieur de Technologie offers a professional licence in Informatique (computer science) alongside civil/industrial/mining engineering degrees, and private institutions (ESGNT, established 2015, and ESGIS) also offer IT-related degrees, with ONI offering a BTS in applications programming. At least three institutions with ICT programmes were identified, above the '<2 institutions' threshold. Revised from 1 to 2 (limited: few institutions, low enrolment); enrolment figures are not published, so this is a conservative one-band increase.
